{"rule": "Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and a new passage of about 250 words in the text field.", "text": "The cup was cold. He drank from it anyway, and she let him, and neither of them said anything about it.

After a while she stood and took the kettle to the stove. It gave her something to do with her back to him, which she suspected he would want, and when she turned around again he had put the letter in his shirt pocket and buttoned the flap over it.

"How long did he have?" he asked.

"The doctor said a month. He got nearly three."

"Stubborn."

"Yes."

She set the kettle on and stood by it. The wind had dropped a little. Through the window the light was going out of the yard the way it did in that season, all at once and without ceremony, and she could see the shape of his truck and beyond it the fence line running off toward the creek.

"He talked about the place," she said. "Toward the end. Not about you. About the place. The lower field, and the well that used to go dry in August. He wanted to know if it still did."

"It does."

"I told him I didn't know."

Aldous turned his cup a quarter turn on the table and looked at it.

"He could have written sooner," he said.

"He could have."

"So could I."

The kettle began to make its small beginning noise. She did not move to it yet. She had learned that too, from her own quiet man: that there is a moment before the boil when you leave things be."}
